turns.question: How would you explain cloud computing to your grandparents?
turns.answer: So basically the biggest problem was that two nurses could allocate the same bed at the same moment, because each request read the free bed and then saved it. First I tried to check again before saving, but the problem still happened when requests were very close. Then I read about database transactions and I used select_for_update inside a transaction so the row is locked while one request is allocating it. I tested it by writing a small script that sends twenty requests at the same time, and after the change only one of them got the bed and the others got a clear message. It was the hardest bug in the project and I learned that you cannot trust a check that is done outside the transaction.
